title: Communicating January requirements to parents clearly
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals on telling parents exactly what is needed for January reopening, so the first week is calm and nobody is surprised.
body:
The first week of January is easier or harder depending on what parents were told in November. Families who know the reporting date, the amount due, and what to bring arrive prepared. Families who heard a half-message arrive anxious, and some do not arrive at all.

A single clear communication, sent early and repeated once, removes most of that friction.

What every parent needs to know

The essentials

  • Reporting date and time, for day scholars and boarders separately
  • Fee balance and the January fee structure, with how to pay
  • Uniform and boarding requirements
  • Books and stationery needed, and what the school supplies
  • Medical or other forms to be completed
  • Who to contact with questions, and when

Separate what is required from what is optional

Many parent complaints come from not knowing which items are mandatory. List required items first, then optional ones, and state a cost wherever there is one. Anything that is not stated in writing becomes a dispute later.

Anticipate the questions: Add a short FAQ to the message covering the three questions you expect most, such as late reporting, fee instalments, and transfers. It saves your office hundreds of calls.

Timing and channels

Send the full communication in late November, and a shorter reminder about two weeks before reopening. Use a WhatsApp broadcast for reach and the Parent Portal as the place parents can look it up again. Avoid relying on students to carry information home.

Give new families extra care

Parents of incoming Grade 10 learners, especially boarding families, are doing this for the first time. A separate welcome pack that adds orientation details and a contact person for questions reduces anxiety.

Reach every parent with one message.
